messages:
elaine.c: Quick heads-up — FinBlock (Dedicated) asked for a concise post-incident follow-up after yesterday's embeddings degradation. They want: a plain-English RCA, confirmed mitigations (what we changed), and the credit/compensation calculation. I drafted a short email + status page blurb below. Can ops/reliability & support sanity-check? I want to send this before EOD PST.

incident-bot: Paging incident 2026-03-14T21:03Z -> incident assigned to @jordan-oncall. Severity: SEV2. Affected service: embeddings.redwood.prod (region-us-west).

jordan-oncall: saw. quick summary from our side: starting ~20:50 UTC models started returning 5xx on the dedicated pool for FinBlock due to a KV cache eviction bug combined with a high-prefix duplication workload. That triggered long tail latency + request retries which exhausted worker slots and led to more 5xx. We rolled a config that increased per-worker cache TTL and disabled a faulty eviction path at 21:05 UTC which restored steady traffic by 21:18 UTC.

samir.p: adding detail on metrics: redis eviction spikes at 20:49:32 UTC, 5xx rate peaked ~20:52, p95 latency jumped from 180ms -> 1.8s. Error budget for their dedicated pool briefly exceeded threshold (alert fired).

mica.s: good timeline. For the customer note we should be explicit about impact window and what to expect in credits. FinBlock had ~6m of elevated error for 2 of their reserved lanes; their billable token volume during the impact window was ~480k tokens.

support-bot: Suggested credit calc: base credit = proportional to failed requests + SLA clause. Proposed quick formula: (affected_token_fraction) * (monthly_commit / 30) * downtime_hours. Need finance confirmation.

elaine.c: here's my draft email to FinBlock (please comment inline). I'm keeping it short and actionable.

```
Subject: Follow-up on yesterday's embeddings interruption — timeline and next steps

Hi Maria,

Thanks again for your patience during yesterday's degradation of embeddings (us-west dedicated pool). We know this impacted your ingestion pipeline and appreciate the details your team shared during the call. Below is a short timeline, what we changed, and next steps including the proposed credit. If you'd like a walk-through we can schedule a 30-min technical review.

Timeline (UTC):
- 20:49 — First metric anomaly: Redis eviction rate spike detected on the dedicated pool.
- 20:50 — Increased 5xx responses and p95 latency observed. We opened an incident and paged on-call.
- 21:05 — Deployed config change: disabled the problematic cache-eviction path and increased per-worker KV TTL.
- 21:18 — Traffic returned to normal error/latency baselines. Monitoring confirmed stability through 21:45.

What we changed:
- Disabled the eviction path in the runtime that caused concurrent cache thrashing under high duplicated-prefix workloads.
- Increased per-worker KV cache TTL to reduce churn during bursty ingestion.
- Added additional guardrails on worker capacity to prevent cascading slot exhaustion.

Preventative actions:
- Patch to the eviction algorithm (deploy planned next week, will be canaried).
- Auto-throttle rule to detect duplicate-prefix bursts and shed non-critical inference requests earlier.
- Post-deploy perf testing with synthetic duplicate-prefix workloads.

Proposed credit (preliminary): equivalent of the proportion of affected committed capacity for the 29-minute impact window. We estimate this to be ~X credits; finance will confirm final figure.

If you'd like, we can join a short call to walk through this and share logs/metrics.

Best,
Elaine C (Redwood Customer Success)
```

jordan-oncall: draft looks solid. A couple of small clarifications so we don't overclaim: the eviction path was disabled as an emergency config rollback, full code-level fix timeline should be 'patch planned next week' (as you wrote). Also change 29-minute to 'about 28 minutes' to align with our exact timestamps (20:49:32 -> 21:17:52).

samir.p: for the credit line we should include the actual number instead of X. My calc (preliminary, awaiting finance): affected_fraction = 2 lanes / 8 reserved lanes = 0.25. Impact_duration_hours = 28 / 3600 = 0.0078. If monthly_commit_usd = $40,000 -> daily = 1333.33 -> hourly ~55.56. Credit_estimate = 55.56 * 0.25 * 0.4667? wait that's messy; simpler: credit_proportion = affected_fraction * (impact_minutes / minutes_in_month). Minutes_in_month ~ 43200. credit_fraction ~ 0.25 * (28/43200) = 0.000162; monthly_credit_usd = 40000 * 0.000162 = ~$6.48. That seems small because monthly commit large; maybe our SLA has minimum rounding; finance to confirm and possibly issue a nominal credit tier.

mica.s: good to flag finance confirm. Also add a short 'what you can expect from us' line: 'final credit confirmation within 3 business days and optional 30-min review call.'

incident-bot: Incident 1992345600 closed by @jordan-oncall at 1992346672. Postmortem scheduled.

elaine.c: revised email below with the changes. Also drafted a suggested status page update and short internal note for PMs. Please sign off.

```
Status page (public):

Title: Partial service disruption — embeddings (us-west)

Summary: Between 20:49 and 21:18 UTC on 2026-03-14, a subset of dedicated embedding pools experienced elevated error rates and increased latency. A configuration rollback and cache-TTL adjustment mitigated the issue and service returned to normal. We are deploying a permanent patch and additional throttling safeguards.

Impact: Affected some dedicated customers in the us-west region; hosted API customers were not materially impacted.

What we're doing: emergency rollback + cache TTL change applied; permanent patch and throttling rule planned; post-deploy testing scheduled.
```

elaine.c: internal customer-success note (short): "FinBlock affected from 20:49–21:18 UTC; prepping credit estimate and scheduling 30-min technical call on request. Finance to confirm final credit within 3 business days."

jordan-oncall: approved. one nit: change 'hosted API customers were not materially impacted' -> 'hosted API customers saw no significant errors' (clearer). :thumbsup:

samir.p: approve from ops; add a line in the customer email offering logs: "We can provide request IDs and timeline slices if helpful."

mica.s: approve from support. I'll own scheduling the optional call and collecting the right dashboard screenshots.

support-bot: Draft credit note for finance handoff: "FinBlock — dedicated pool — 28 minutes of elevated error for 2/8 lanes. Preliminary estimated credit ~$6.50 (subject to SLA rounding/minimums). Please confirm final figure and currency."

elaine.c: thanks all. I'll send this as 'official follow-up' and copy ops and finance. Sending now. Will post final credit confirmation once finance replies.

jordan-oncall: thanks — postmortem thread to follow with root cause analysis and action owners.

mica.s: ping me if customer asks for raw logs; I'll pull snapshots.

elaine.c: final note sent at 1992346420. I'll update this thread with the finance number and link to the postmortem when available. :white_check_mark:
